A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Kinetix/Jax2D research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; Appendices A–M are retained, and v2 adds Appendices N–Q.

before.justification: V1 reports original physics-engine benchmarks, zero-shot and fine-tuning experiments, morphology-control evaluations, and curriculum and representation ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds learnability measurements, observation/action comparisons, cross-embodiment training results, and a lifelong-learning experiment.

M1.justification: The Jax2D engine, entity-based transformer, PPO/SFL training procedure, and reward formulation are retained. The pixel observations and continuous actions newly compared in Appendix O were already supported and described in v1; their evaluation does not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: The 74 handmade levels, S/M/L distributions, and represented task families are retained. Appendix Q adds a lifelong-learning scenario that tests retention after sequential S-to-M-to-S distribution switches. The other added experiments reuse existing levels and morphologies.

E2.justification: Figure 30 newly compares Entity–MultiDiscrete against Entity–Continuous, Pixels–MultiDiscrete, and Pixels–Continuous for learning performance. Figure 31 adds a joint-versus-individual training comparison. Existing DR, PLR, ACCEL, tabula rasa, and Box2D comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendices O–Q introduce substantial new experimental designs: training and evaluating jointly on all 74 handmade tasks, comparing seven jointly trained MuJoCo recreations with individual specialists using 500M versus 100M interactions, and sequential training for 5B S, 1B M, and 1B S interactions. These supplement the retained main protocols; they are not evidence of improved performance under the original zero-shot setting.

E4.justification: New Appendices N–Q examine selected versus random levels' learnability, factorial observation/action choices, transfer from joint training across morphologies, and retention after distribution switches. These substantially extend the original filtering, curriculum, representation, and locomotion analyses.

E5.justification: New Figures 30–31 explicitly report means and standard deviations over five seeds, while the retained main figures continue reporting standard errors. Appendix Q identifies its evidence as a single run. V2 does not document increased replication of the existing experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 29–32 add findings that selected levels maintain much higher learnability, MultiDiscrete actions outperform Continuous actions in the new multitask experiment, joint training has morphology-dependent benefits, and M performance declines after returning to S training. Existing benchmark results are retained; the additions provide substantial new outcomes under separately specified conditions.

T1.justification: The MDP and learnability definitions, reward equation, and Appendix A physics derivations and equations are unchanged. V2 adds no substantive theorem, proof, or mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly qualifies the agent's physical reasoning capabilities as occurring 'in 2D space.' This tightens the stated scope, while the four principal contributions and the zero-shot and fine-tuning claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new appendices interpret the interface ablation as supporting the chosen observations and actions, discuss joint training's transfer and sample-efficiency tradeoffs, and identify possible forgetting or plasticity loss after distribution switches. These add specific qualifications without substantially revising the main discussion or conclusions.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly reports approximately 7, 9, and 14 hours for one billion training interactions on S, M, and L using one L40S GPU. This adds practical resource information; the existing architecture descriptions, hyperparameter tables, and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to PGX, Jumanji, Navix, hindsight experience replay, and functional reward encodings, and removes the Continual Backprop and Enhanced POET references. The main positioning relative to XLand, physics engines, and generalist robotics remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, particularly in related work, adds explanatory sentences and cross-references, and extends the appendix roadmap. It also adds acknowledgements and the conference header. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 29–32, relocates Figure 4, and adds clearer y-axis markings to Figure 5's individual-task panels. Existing tables and most figures retain their presentation. Figure 32 has a caption mismatch: it describes S and M panels, but only the M panel is displayed.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for its design choices through the observation/action ablation and adds useful evidence about curriculum selection and joint training, alongside concrete runtime information. These improve supporting analysis and transparency while the central study remains stable. The lifelong-learning addition has limited evidential strength because it uses one run and Figure 32 omits the S panel described in its caption.
